title: a tuple-typed array of Results is consumed through an index read, like the array literal
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx §Configuration (the worked example this case is written from): '`arr[i]!` does not silently change meaning, and it compiles when `arr` holds Results. The `| undefined` an index read adds under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is not the author's — the option widens the *access*, never the container's element type — so it is seen through, and `arr[i]!` means there what `!` means everywhere else.' The annotated tuple type is the point: the container's declared type still carries the Result channel, so the transfer is real rather than a fiction. The negative half of that distinction is 09-foreign-calls/foreign-module-without-a-trust-marker, where a LIFTED foreign Result goes into a plainly-typed `string[]` and the channel is dropped on the way in — there the array does not hold the channel and the Result is genuinely discarded. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-28: this case did NOT move when `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` was turned on, and that is the measurement it contributes. A tuple read at a CONSTANT in-bounds index is not widened by the option, so `pair[0]` stayed `Result<string, Missing>` while its array-literal sibling became `Result<string, Missing> | undefined`. It is the control that shows the two cases were never duplicates.
